children: Indian defence stocks extended their decline for a fifth consecutive session on Wednesday. The Nifty India Defence index fell more than 1 percent despite HSBC highlighting strong earnings visibility from a multi-year defence spending cycle.

The defence index was down 1.02 percent at 9,050.45 around mid-morning, even as the broader market traded higher. At 10:32 am, the Sensex was up 336 points, or 0.45 percent, at 74,340, while the Nifty 50 gained 110 points to 23,229.

The latest decline takes the Nifty India Defence index's five-session fall to around 9.7 percent. The index had already lost 8.5 percent over the preceding four sessions. The losing streak follows a run-up that culminated on September 8, when the defence index jumped 2.5 percent after the Defence Acquisition Council cleared acquisition proposals worth around Rs 1.10 lakh crore across the Army, Navy and Air Force.

Selling on Wednesday was broad-based. MTAR Technologies was the biggest loser among the stocks in the index, falling 4.4 percent to Rs 6,639, while Apollo Micro Systems declined 4.2 percent to Rs 370.35.

Solar Industries India fell 3.1 percent to Rs 18,655, AxisCades Technologies declined 3.1 percent to Rs 1,663.90 and Paras Defence and Space Technologies shed 2.8 percent to Rs 1,302.10. Mishra Dhatu Nigam and Dynamatic Technologies were down more than 2 percent each.

Among the larger defence names, Hindustan Aeronautics (HAL) declined 1.2 percent to Rs 4,637.90, Bharat Dynamics fell 1.3 percent to Rs 1,120.10 and Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders slipped 0.7 percent to Rs 2,221. However, Bharat Electronics (BEL) bucked the trend with a 0.5 percent gain to Rs 384.90, while Astra Microwave Products rose 0.8 percent to Rs 1,606.90.

The continued weakness comes even as HSBC expects a multi-year increase in Indian defence spending to provide strong earnings visibility for the sector, supported by domestic procurement and rising exports. The brokerage expects the order cycle to be driven by defence electronics, aerospace, missiles and other defence systems, as well as unmanned systems.

HSBC initiated coverage on HAL and BEL with 'buy' ratings. It started Bharat Dynamics, Astra Microwave Products, Data Patterns and Solar Industries with 'hold' ratings; it initiated Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders with a 'reduce' rating.

The recent DAC approvals had strengthened expectations of a sizeable domestic order pipeline. About 98 percent of the Rs 1.10 lakh crore of acquisition proposals approved on September 7 were earmarked for Indian industry, covering equipment across the three armed forces.
